text:
sam_support: FYI Acme hit us — p95/p99 spike on function-calling endpoints after yesterday's router push. They reported p95 ~600-800ms (used to be ~120ms). Customer is on a Dedicated route and said schema-heavy calls. Ticket: https://acme.ticket/1234

maria_oncall: copy. Can you paste a repro request (trimmed) + which model + route config? Any recent config toggles for JSON schema validation or tool routing?

sam_support: here's a minimal curl they gave:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large-1","mode":"function_call","input":"Summarize...","tools":[{"name":"search","schema":{/*big schema*/}}]}'
```
and a snippet from their client-side timings: "total: 870ms, server: 810ms, client pre: 30ms"

jia_engineer: thanks. Any chance structured-output validation (strict JSON schema) was enabled for that customer? That and the router's tool dispatch path can add sync CPU on the request path.

sam_support: yes — we toggled "enforce_schema": true for their dedicated route last Monday per sales ask. Config excerpt attached:
```json
{
  "route_id": "ded-acme-01",
  "model": "rw-large-1",
  "enforce_schema": true,
  "router_mode": "single-threaded",
  "tool_router": {"enabled": true, "validation": "sync"}
}
```

deploy-bot: deploy: router-service@2026.03.15-18:22 deployed to prod (router-v2). CI checks passed.

nate_engruntime: ok this looks like the culprit — sync validation + single-threaded router. JSON schema validation for big tool schemas can be O(n) CPU per request and currently runs inline before generation. Quick mitigation: flip validation to async or use a lightweight schema check to short-circuit. Can someone run a canary by toggling validation=false for that route? Command: `ri routes update ded-acme-01 --enforce_schema=false --validation=async`

mia_support: can we do a controlled change? flip on a single host or subset of traffic to be safe.

nate_engruntime: yep — will put a canary at 5% traffic on router-hosts a/b. I'll also enable a flag to batch schema validations every 100ms window to amortize cost.

sam_support: applied canary flag at 18:35. I'll monitor customer metrics.

sam_support (18:49): quick update from Acme: after canary p95 dropped to ~140ms and p99 to ~260ms. They report normal UX now.

jia_engineer: great. Follow-ups: 1) change default router config to use async validation for large schemas, 2) add a size-threshold to use lightweight check, 3) add observability span to measure schema-validation time per request so we have exact breakdowns in Console.

maria_oncall: filing a post-escalation task for infra backlog — include repro, config, and the canary commands + numbers. Also schedule a short retro with DS to see if any QA could catch this on staging.

sam_support: thanks all — I'll message the customer and close the urgent ticket, keep the canary running until patch lands. :thumbsup:

nate_engruntime: I'll open PR with batching + async default. ETA EOD.

mia_support: adding this thread to the incident summary doc.

sam_support: closing loop — customer confirmed degradation resolved, will reopen if anything else.
